A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same research, renamed from WPT to GSA. Their methods, experiments, tables and appendices can be matched reliably despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results on DMControl and Meta-World, including benchmark performance, continual task adaptation and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds distribution-shift diagnostics, component fine-tuning experiments and further baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The 280M-parameter RSSM, action padding, reconstruction/KL objective, feature-based retrieval, experience rehearsal and scheduled switching between behavior-cloned and RL policies are retained. Algorithm 1 matches apart from naming and cross-references; the new selective fine-tuning experiments are ablations.

E1.justification: Both retain the same offline corpora, reported 22 locomotion and 50 manipulation benchmark tasks, hard-exploration tests and Ant adaptation sequence. The tasks used in v2's additional comparisons and diagnostics were already represented in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds iVideoGPT and Diffusion Policy as evaluated comparators, plus a comparison containing externally pre-trained DreamerV3 (Figures 4, 9 and 10). The world-model comparison uses baseline results attributed to the iVideoGPT paper. Existing R3M, UDS, ExPLORe, JSRL-BC, scratch-training and PackNet comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce Wasserstein-distance evaluation and controls comparing full-model, encoder/decoder-only and latent-dynamics-only fine-tuning. Existing benchmark budgets and Table 5 settings remain unchanged. The added world-model comparison explicitly uses literature baselines with reward shaping and expert-buffer initialization, while GSA lacks those treatments.

E4.justification: v2 adds a Shelf Place distribution-mismatch analysis (Figure 2) and a Quadruped Walk component fine-tuning study (Figure 8). Existing component and uncertainty-reward ablations are largely retained or relocated, but the individual Quadruped Walk and Shelf Place component panels and the Soccer uncertainty-reward panel disappear.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports three seeds in the six-task Figure 4 caption. v2 states three random seeds for each task and documents 72-by-3 runs in Appendix F. This broadens the disclosed scope without establishing additional runs. The existing 95% confidence-interval and IQM reporting practices remain.

E6.justification: v2 adds results against iVideoGPT and Diffusion Policy, distribution-distance measurements and selective fine-tuning curves, while omitting several individual ablation results. Tables 2–4 retain their numerical entries. The 102.8% headline is a relative re-expression of retained aggregate scores, rather than evidence of improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: Appendix B newly presents three propositions and proof arguments concerning retrieval-distance reduction, catastrophic-forgetting mitigation and execution-guidance performance. These introduce assumptions and a performance bound of alpha times delta divided by one minus gamma, beyond v1's definitions and training equations.

C1.justification: v2 makes distribution-shift diagnosis an explicit headline contribution, extends the performance claim to other pre-trained world-model methods and removes dataset release from the contribution list. The central claims of sample-efficient RL and task adaptation using non-curated data remain.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds substantive boundaries concerning in-domain data, unestablished generalization to new embodiments/configurations and RSSM scaling limitations. v2 also interprets the new comparisons and fine-tuning study as evidence for reusing offline data during adaptation and updating the full world model, extending v1's discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds hardware specifications, pre-training/fine-tuning timings and total GPU-hour estimates. Existing hyperparameters and implementation listings remain. However, v2 omits v1's R3M ResNet-18 specification, hard-Cheetah reward-construction description and dataset open-sourcing statement; the PDFs do not establish an actual withdrawal of data access.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against action-free and video-based world-model pre-training and adds an unsupervised-RL discussion in Appendix C. New citations support these comparisons and the theory, while parts of v1's broad vision/language-scaling motivation disappear. Existing generalist-agent and world-model discussions are partly relocated.

P1.justification: The title, method name, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the method and experimental narrative are rewritten. Contributions are reorganized, related work and impact discussion move partly into appendices, and an appendix contents page and several dedicated sections are introduced.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text from two columns to one, expands the method schematic and adds diagnostic, baseline-comparison and fine-tuning figures. It merges the aggregate and six-task comparisons, relocates IQM and uncertainty-reward displays, and reduces several panel sets. These are extensive visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The distribution diagnostic and component fine-tuning study better support v1's largely intuitive explanation, while explicit in-domain and generalization limitations improve claim calibration. Additional world-model comparisons broaden assessment. The gain is limited by differently configured, literature-derived baselines, omitted ablation panels and implementation details, and theoretical assumptions not established for the implemented guidance procedure.
